svg.title: State
svg.desc: State. Let an object change its behaviour when its state changes by delegating to state objects instead of growing switch statements. Step 1, A switch in every method: pay(), ship() and cancel() each switch on status: 12 branches, and a new state edits all three. Step 2, One class per state: Each state becomes a class with its own pay(), ship() and cancel(); Order delegates to its state. Step 3, The state decides: pay() takes the order from Pending to Paid and ship() to Shipped; cancel() in Shipped is refused. Step 4, A new state, one class: OnHold is one new class plus one changed line in Pending; Order and the other states are untouched.

g.text: pay(), ship() and cancel() each switch on status: 12 branches, and a new state edits all three.
Each state becomes a class with its own pay(), ship() and cancel(); Order delegates to its state.
pay() takes the order from Pending to Paid and ship() to Shipped; cancel() in Shipped is refused.
OnHold is one new class plus one changed line in Pending; Order and the other states are untouched.
4 states × 3 methods = 12 branches, spread over three switch statements
A new state edits every switch, and a missed case fails silently
→ Paid returns the next state, and Order moves to it
✗ pay first refuses: the state stays
vs Strategy: the client picks a strategy; states replace each other
Shared: a state with no fields needs only one instance (Singleton, Flyweight)
As data: transition tables, statecharts (Harel 1987), XState
In systems: a circuit breaker and a saga orchestrator are state machines
